span: Proves the full Birch--Swinnerton-Dyer leading-term formula for every elliptic curve over $\mathbb Q$ whose full $q$-power Selmer group has corank zero or one for some prime $q$, including finiteness of the Tate--Shafarevich group.
Exact Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer Formula from Low Selmer Corank
whose full $q$-power Selmer group has corank zero or one for some prime $q$
The two-primary Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer formula in Selmer corank at most one
Proves that every Dirichlet $L$-function, including $\zeta(s)$, is zero-free in $\Re s>7/8$, resolving the quasi-Riemann hypothesis.
The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis: A Zero-Free Half-Plane $\Re s>7/8$
A companion gives a different proof of the zero-free half-plane $\Re s>11/12$.
The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis (alternate $11/12$ proof)
The same half-plane is zero-free for every finite-order Hecke $L$-function over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$.
Uniform exclusion of Landau--Siegel zeros
Proves that no algorithm decides whether an integer-coefficient polynomial in an arbitrary number of variables has a rational zero, resolving Hilbert's tenth problem over $\mathbb Q$ negatively.
Hilbert’s tenth over $\mathbb Q$
analytic ranks zero and one each have density $1/2$
Analytic density and 2-converse
and the mean analytic rank tends to $1/2$.
Mean analytic rank
Reconstructs function fields of transcendence degree at least two over algebraically closed constants from $K^{\mathrm M}_1/\ell$, $K^{\mathrm M}_2/\ell$, and their product.
Reconstruction of Function Fields from Mod-$\ell$ Milnor $K$-Theory
These data recover the perfect closure and constants when $\ell$ differs from the characteristic, and the original field and its named base in equal characteristic.
Reconstruction from Milnor $K$-theory modulo the characteristic
Also proves Bogomolov--Pop reconstruction from abelian-by-central pro-$\ell$ Galois data away from the characteristic.
The Bogomolov-Pop reconstruction theorem

Every continuous odd absolutely irreducible two-dimensional $2$-adic representation of $G_{\mathbb Q}$ unramified outside finitely many primes occurs in a completed Hecke algebra at some odd tame level.
Unrestricted pro-modularity

Also proves classical modularity up to Tate twist for irreducible odd representations with these finiteness conditions that are de Rham at $2$ with distinct Hodge--Tate weights, resolving the dyadic Fontaine--Mazur case without residual restrictions.
Fontaine–Mazur modularity at the prime 2

Proves that the normalized ordered logarithms of the prime factors of $p-1$, counted with multiplicity, converge jointly to the Poisson--Dirichlet law $\mathrm{PD}(1)$ as $p$ ranges uniformly over primes up to $x$ and $x\to\infty$.
The Poisson-Dirichlet law for prime predecessors
It also proves that infinitely many integers $n$ have more than $n^{1-\varepsilon}$ totient preimages, for every $\varepsilon>0$.
Weighted dilation graphs, smooth shifted primes and totient fibers

Proves the restricted geometric Langlands equivalence for connected reductive groups on smooth projective connected curves over $\overline{\mathbb F}_q$ under the four stated Lie-theoretic characteristic hypotheses.
Restricted geometric Langlands
Over arbitrary algebraically closed fields of characteristic $p>0$, the same conclusion holds assuming additionally that $p$ is very good for the group and $p\nmid |W_G|$.

Over global function fields, proves Ramanujan at every place for globally generic cuspidal representations of split adjoint absolutely simple exceptional groups, without characteristic or ramification-depth restrictions
Temperedness at ramified places for globally generic exceptional groups
and at every unramified place for cuspidal representations of split adjoint absolutely simple groups with a generic unramified component.
Unramified Arthur filtration

Assuming the finite-level Ramanujan--Arthur decomposition, constructs global Arthur enhancements of occurring cuspidal excursion parameters for split connected semisimple groups at full finite level, recovering the given parameters by diagonal specialization on the entire Weil group, including inertia.
Global Arthur Enhancements of Cuspidal Excursion Parameters
Proves Haar equidistribution without escape of mass for complete volume-weighted torus packets from totally real fields
Equidistribution of Prime-Degree Torus Packets with Arbitrary Local Type
arbitrary-order Picard packets in primitive quartic fields
Equidistribution of primitive quartic torus packets for arbitrary orders
maximal-order ideal-class packets in primitive sextic fields
Equidistribution of Primitive Sextic Torus Packets
Proves the abelian Zilber--Pink conjecture over $\overline{\mathbb Q}$: every irreducible subvariety has finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties relative to its smallest containing torsion coset.
Abelian Zilber–Pink
It also proves the full curve case in the Siegel threefold $\mathcal A_2$ for Hodge-generic curves defined over $\overline{\mathbb Q}$, without boundary or reduction assumptions.
Proves the Margulis--Platonov conjecture over every global field
The Margulis–Platonov conjecture over number fields
including function fields of characteristic two.
The Margulis--Platonov conjecture over global function fields

Proves that rational points on every smooth proper geometrically connected curve of genus at least two over a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$ correspond bijectively to conjugacy classes of sections of its full arithmetic \'etale fundamental group.
p-adic section conjecture
It also proves Grothendieck's section conjecture over $\mathbb Q$ for the modular curves $X_0(N)$ and $X_1(N)$ of genus at least two.
Proves the infinitude assertion in Artin's primitive root conjecture for every integer $a$ that is neither $-1$ nor a square.
Primitive roots for every admissible integer base
Proves the rational Hodge conjecture for every complex CM abelian variety, in every dimension and codimension.
The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties
Through Milne's theorems, this also gives the Tate conjecture for all abelian varieties over finite fields and the Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties in every characteristic.
Proves Campana's orbifold Iitaka subadditivity conjecture for smooth Fujiki-class-$\mathcal C$ manifolds with rational simple-normal-crossing boundaries.
Orbifold and logarithmic subadditivity
proves Popa's inequality $\bar\kappa(U)\ge\kappa(F)+\max\{\bar\kappa(V),\operatorname{Var}(f)\}$, where variation measures the whole geometric generic fiber
Whole-fiber variation

Using logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity, proves log abundance in every dimension for normal compact K\"ahler log canonical pairs with effective rational boundary: an analytically nef $\mathbb Q$-Cartier adjoint is semiample.
Log abundance for compact Kähler spaces
It also proves projective log abundance over every algebraically closed field of characteristic zero
Log abundance in characteristic zero
and the effective Iitaka fibration conjecture for smooth projective varieties of nonnegative Kodaira dimension in that setting.
Uniform pluricanonical Iitaka fibrations

A further result resolves the finite-rational-coefficient index conjecture for connected projective semi-log-canonical log Calabi--Yau pairs over such fields in each fixed dimension and for each fixed finite set of rational boundary coefficients, with a uniform index independent of the number of components.
Uniform indices for semi-log-canonical log Calabi--Yau pairs

Proves log abundance for projective log canonical threefold pairs over algebraically closed fields of characteristic $p>3$ when the effective boundary is rational and the $\mathbb Q$-Cartier adjoint is nef of numerical dimension one.
Log abundance in numerical dimension one for threefolds in positive characteristic
The adjoint is semiample, without requiring the original variety to be terminal or $\mathbb Q$-factorial.
Abundance in numerical dimension one for terminal threefolds in positive characteristic
Proves numerical semiampleness for nef adjoints $K_X+B+M$ with $K_X+B$ pseudo-effective and $M$ nef rational, for projective klt rational pairs over algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields
Projective numerical semiampleness
smooth compact K\"ahler rational klt simple-normal-crossing pairs, using Bott--Chern cohomology in the latter case
Compact Kähler numerical semiampleness
projective generalized log canonical rational pairs over such fields admit minimal models for pseudo-effective adjoints and Mori fiber spaces otherwise, with nef b-data fixed
Generalized log canonical Q-pairs
every singular complex algebraic klt germ of dimension $n\ge2$, with zero boundary, has normalized volume at most $2(n-1)^n$
Gap in every dimension
Equality holds precisely for an analytic ordinary double point.
Dimension-four normalized-volume gap
Proves Nagata's strict inequality $\sum_i m_i<d\sqrt r$ for every nonzero effective plane curve of degree $d$ through $r\ge10$ very general complex points, with arbitrary multiplicities $m_i$.
Plane-curve Nagata conjecture

It also proves maximal multipoint Seshadri constants $(L^n/r)^{1/n}$ for every smooth polarized projective variety of dimension $n\ge2$ and all sufficiently large $r$: at very general points over $\mathbb C$
Maximal Multipoint Seshadri Constants in Higher Dimensions
and at the geometric generic tuple over any algebraically closed field of positive characteristic.
Maximal multipoint Seshadri constants in positive characteristic

Proves the strong hyperk\"ahler SYZ conjecture: every holomorphic line bundle with nonzero nef isotropic first Chern class on a compact irreducible holomorphic symplectic K\"ahler manifold is semiample.
Strong hyperkähler SYZ
It also proves that every projective Lagrangian fibration with normal projective base has projective space as its base, in every dimension and deformation type.
Projective-space bases

Constructs a smooth projective complex fourfold with large fundamental group whose universal cover contains no positive-dimensional compact analytic subvariety but is neither Stein nor holomorphically convex.
A projective fourfold with large fundamental group and non-Stein universal cover
A separate smooth projective complex surface already disproves unrestricted Shafarevich holomorphic convexity in dimension two.
A surface counterexample to Shafarevich holomorphic convexity
Constructs a polynomial in four complex variables that is not a coordinate but becomes one after adjoining a single variable, disproving the Stable Coordinate conjecture in four variables.
A stable coordinate that is not a coordinate in four variables
Every fiber is affine three-space, yet none of its embeddings is rectifiable, also disproving the Abhyankar--Sathaye conjecture even when all fibers are affine spaces.
An explicit noncoordinate polynomial with affine three-space zero fibre

A splitting of the tangent bundle of a compact K\"ahler manifold into two integrable holomorphic subbundles induces a compatible product decomposition of its universal cover, proving the two-summand form of Beauville's splitting conjecture.
Kähler universal-cover splitting
On smooth rationally connected projective manifolds, both summands are automatically integrable, establishing H\"oring's conjecture and the corresponding product decomposition.
Integrability on rationally connected manifolds
Proves Toda's Gepner conjecture for every smooth complex quintic threefold, constructing a numerical Bridgeland stability condition with the prescribed phase shift $2/5$.
Gepner stability on quintic threefolds

Also constructs numerical Bridgeland stability conditions at every sufficiently large volume on all smooth projective complex threefolds with trivial canonical bundle, with the exact ordinary and square-root-Todd central charges.
Prescribed large-volume charges

Proves termination of every existing generalized log canonical flip sequence on globally Weil $\mathbb Q$-factorial compact K\"ahler fourfolds, with rational boundary, fixed rational analytically nef b-data, and projective small flip diagrams with the prescribed ample signs.
Termination of generalized log canonical flips on compact Kähler fourfolds
Also proves termination of arbitrary permitted minimal model programs for projective log canonical fourfolds with rational boundary in characteristic zero.
Log canonical fourfold termination
Proves Campana's abelianity conjecture: special compact K\"ahler manifolds have virtually abelian fundamental groups.
Special compact Kähler abelianity
establishes the same conclusion for order-two root orbifolds of smooth projective complex fourfolds along one nonempty smooth connected divisor
A conditional abelianity theorem for special fourfold pairs with a half-weight divisor
every finite-dimensional complex linear representation of the fundamental group has virtually nilpotent image of class at most two
Two-step monodromy
Proves the Koll\'ar--Pardon conjecture: the semialgebraic universal covers of connected normal projective complex varieties are exactly products $D\times\mathbb C^m\times F$
Semialgebraic universal covers
with $D$ bounded symmetric and $F$ simply connected, normal, and projective.
Bounded-domain symmetry
Disproves Zariski's multiplicity conjecture by constructing reduced holomorphic hypersurface germs that are ambiently homeomorphic but have different multiplicities.
Multiplicities two and three
The examples include hypersurfaces in $\mathbb C^4$ with isolated critical points and multiplicities four and five.
Multiplicities four and five
Proves the full ordinary unreduced descendant Virasoro conjecture for smooth complete intersections in complex projective space, in every genus and curve class with arbitrary cohomology insertions.
Virasoro Constraints for Projective Complete Intersections
The constraints also pass from any smooth projective complex base satisfying them to the projectivization of every algebraic vector bundle of rank at least two, and hence to projective-bundle towers.
Virasoro Constraints under Projectivization
Proves the finite-rational-coefficient form of Shokurov’s bounded-klt-complement conjecture for $\epsilon$-lc complex Fano-type pairs with nef anti-log-canonical divisor.
Bounded klt complements

For $\epsilon$-lc Fano contractions over any algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, it gives klt complements near every base point, with index bounded only by dimension and positive rational $\epsilon$.
Uniform Cartier sections
If $X$ is a smooth connected complex projective variety and $-K_X$ admits a smooth Hermitian metric with nonnegative curvature, then $H^0(X,-mK_X)\ne0$ for some $m>0$.
Smooth semipositivity
Thus smooth semipositivity forces a nonzero section of a positive tensor power of the anticanonical bundle in every dimension.
Resolves the existence part of Koebe's circle-domain conjecture: every domain in the Riemann sphere is conformally equivalent to a domain whose complementary components are round disks or points.
Koebe’s circle-domain conjecture

It also proves that circle domains with conformally removable boundary are rigid, meaning every conformal equivalence to another circle domain is M\"obius, establishing this direction of the He--Schramm conjecture.
Removable boundaries and rigidity
Proves Brennan's conjecture: for every conformal bijection $\phi$ from a simply connected plane domain onto the disk, $|\phi'|^s$ is area-integrable for $4/3<s<4$.
Brennan’s conjecture
A strict bound $B_b(-1)<1/4$ for bounded univalent functions disproves Kraetzer's prediction at that parameter.
Strict inverse-first-power bound
Resolves the Kakeya maximal conjecture in three dimensions
3D Kakeya maximal conjecture
and the Hausdorff-dimension conjecture in four.
4D Kakeya Hausdorff dimension
Constructs polynomials with $N$ consecutive coefficients in $\{-1,1\}$ whose modulus is $(1+o(1))\sqrt N$ uniformly on the entire unit circle
Ultraflat real Littlewood polynomials
Their binary merit factors tend to infinity, disproving Turyn's bounded-merit-factor conjecture.
Nearly minimal maxima and positive minima of Littlewood polynomials
Proves the diagonal Fourier extension conjecture for positively curved surfaces in three dimensions.
Diagonal Fourier extension

For every compact smooth positively curved surface $\Sigma\subset\mathbb R^3$, including surfaces with boundary, the extension operator is bounded from $L^p(\Sigma)$ to $L^p(\mathbb R^3)$ for every $p>3$.
Sphere restriction
Proves almost-everywhere convergence $e^{it\Delta}f\to f$ as $t\downarrow0$ for every $f\in H^{n/(2(n+1))}(\mathbb R^n)$ and every dimension $n\ge2$.
Higher-dimensional endpoint convergence
including the planar endpoint $H^{1/3}$.
Planar endpoint convergence
Proves maximal and annular $r$-variation bounds, for every $r>2$, from complex $L^3(\mathbb R^2)\times L^3(\mathbb R^2)$ to $L^{3/2}(\mathbb R^2)$.
An $L^3$ bound for the dyadic triangular Hilbert form
The maximal estimate controls both hard truncation endpoints and gives almost-everywhere and norm convergence.
The maximal triangular Hilbert transform at the symmetric point
Pairing with a third input settles the triangular Hilbert transform estimate at the symmetric $L^3\times L^3\times L^3$ point.
Annular variation of the triangular Hilbert transform at the symmetric point

For every fixed $q\in(0,1)$, constructs compact subsets of $[0,1]$ with measure arbitrarily close to one containing no translated and nontrivially dilated copy of $\{q^n:n\ge1\}$, with dilations of either sign.
The geometric case of the Erd\H{o}s similarity conjecture
This resolves the geometric-progression case of the Erd\H{o}s similarity conjecture for every ratio.
The dyadic case of the Erdős similarity conjecture
Resolves the symmetric and nonsymmetric geometric Mahler conjectures in every dimension
General Mahler conjecture
all equality cases classified
Symmetric Mahler equality cases
For $n\ge2$, every symmetric polar product $K\times K^\circ$ in dimension $2n$ has Gromov width $4$.
Symplectic balls in polar products
Proves Petty's projection-volume conjecture in the remaining dimensions $n\ge4$: ellipsoids uniquely minimize projection-body volume at fixed body volume.
Petty’s projection-volume conjecture
In contrast, products of simplices exceed Brannen's proposed simplex maximum for normalized projection-body volume by an exponential factor in every sufficiently large dimension.
Product counterexample to simplex maximum
Also establishes the full Lutwak--Petty projection inequalities.
Resolves the planar and bounded-treewidth cases of the Gupta--Newman--Rabinovich--Sinclair conjecture.
Planar graph embeddings
distortion depending only on treewidth for bounded-treewidth graphs
Bounded-treewidth embeddings

Proves that the triangular lattice minimizes the lower limit of energy per particle for every nonnegative completely monotone potential of squared distance among locally finite planar configurations of centered-disk density one.
Universal optimality
It also minimizes unit-background renormalized Riesz energies for $0<s<2$ and Coulomb energy
Coulomb renormalized energy
Every convex body in $\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, admits a lattice covering of density at most $Cn\log n$
Single-lattice covering bound
centrally symmetric examples in every sufficiently large dimension require at least $cn\log n$ even without the lattice restriction, for absolute $c,C>0$.
Translative covering densities
Disproves the Projected Lax conjecture: some hyperbolicity cones are not spectrahedral shadows.
A nonspectrahedral hyperbolicity cone
The examples admit no exact finite affine semidefinite lift, regardless of the number of auxiliary variables or the real coefficients used.
Hyperbolicity Cones Without Semidefinite Lifts
Determines the least distortion of embedding edit distance on words of length at most $d$ into real $\ell_1$: it is $\exp(\Theta(\sqrt{\log d\,\log\log d}))$.
Matching bounds
Covers the entire closed regular tetrahedron by finitely many cylinders with compact triangular perpendicular bases whose total area is less than half its smallest orthogonal projection area.
Angular cylinder covers
Proves Khot's Unique Games Conjecture.
Unique Games theorem
Independent direct reductions also establish NP-hardness, on unweighted graphs, of approximation beyond the Goemans--Williamson ratio for Max-Cut
Optimal Max-Cut hardness
below factor two for Vertex Cover
Factor-two Vertex Cover hardness
and within any fixed constant factor for Min-UnCut and directed feedback vertex set.
Constant-factor Min-UnCut hardness
and within any fixed constant factor for Min-UnCut and directed feedback vertex set.
Directed feedback vertex set hardness
Gives deterministic algorithms using $2^{O((\log(L+2))^2)}$ bit operations, for complete binary input length $L$, for ordinary mean-payoff games and two separate extensions.
Deterministic algorithm
the nonnegative expectation-of-liminf value set in turn-based stochastic games
Turn-Based Stochastic Mean-Payoff Games in Deterministic Quasipolynomial Time
the winning set for nonnegative liminf mean payoff conjoined with parity
Mean-payoff parity games in quasipolynomial time
Proves $\omega\le9/4$ over $\mathbb C$, giving $O_\varepsilon(n^{9/4+\varepsilon})$ arithmetic operations for square matrix multiplication.
Exponent at most $9/4$ over $\mathbb C$
In characteristic zero, some inner dimension $n^a$ with $a>0.465$ permits $n^{2+o(1)}$ rectangular multiplication.
Earlier complex and rectangular bounds
Further square bounds give $\omega<2.258$ outside finitely many positive characteristics and $\omega<2.371054886006746$ over every fixed field.
Staggered extraction over every field
Establishes a randomized competitive ratio $O(\log^2(k+1))$ for $k$-server on every metric space, matching the worst-case lower-bound order.
Squared-logarithmic randomized k-server

On finite rational metrics, a uniform implementation has polynomial preprocessing and per-request bit cost in the input length and $\log(t+1)$ at request $t$, with a finite instance-dependent additive movement constant.
Uniform computation
Gives a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for counting perfect matchings in arbitrary finite simple graphs, with exact detection of zero counts.
Perfect-matching FPRAS

Also proves the perfect-matching entropy conjecture of Anari, Oveis Gharan, and Vinzant, bounding the maximum entropy of a matching law at every feasible edge-marginal vector in a loopless labelled multigraph, including boundary points.
Entropy and face dimension
Gives a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for counting common integer bases of two integral polymatroids of equal total rank, supplied by exact rank-value oracles.
An FPRAS for Common Integer Polymatroid Bases with Binary Capacities
For matroids presented by independence oracles, the results also cover common independent sets of prescribed, unrestricted, or maximum cardinality, even when the ranks differ.
Approximate counting of common bases of two matroids
For nonnegative integer matrices with prescribed row and column sums, gives exact uniform sampling in expected polynomial bit time and almost-uniform sampling in worst-case polynomial bit time.
Exact uniform sampling
Also gives a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for counting such tables with arbitrary individual cell bounds, including structural zeros, with polynomial cost on every execution.
Cell-bounded counting FPRAS

For each characteristic, constructs in deterministic polynomial bit time a polynomial-dimensional matrix tuple detecting every nonzero division-free noncommutative formula of bounded size over any field of that characteristic.
Uniform Matrix Hitting Points in Every Positive Characteristic
Rational formulas over $\mathbb Q$ also admit polynomial-size hitting lists whenever they have a defined rational-matrix evaluation.
Rational-formula hitting lists
Proves that approximating Uniform Sparsest Cut within any fixed constant factor is NP-hard, even with nonnegative rational capacities and unit demands.
Constant-factor hardness
The Goemans--Linial semidefinite relaxation also has integrality gaps of order at least $\sqrt{\log n}/(\log\log n)^3$, approaching the square-root-logarithmic upper bound.
Near-square-root logarithmic integrality gaps
Proves the Courtade--Kumar conjecture: among Boolean functions of independent uniform bits, a single coordinate retains the most mutual information after independent bit-flip noise.
Sharp binary-information contraction
The Hellinger conjecture is also proved for every Boolean output bias and noise correlation.
Arbitrary-bias Hellinger contraction
A stronger theorem treats randomized binary summaries at fixed initial information.
At every fixed deletion probability in $(0,1)$, reconstructing an arbitrary length-$n$ binary string requires $n^{\Omega(\log\log n)}$ independent traces, ruling out polynomial-sample reconstruction.
Quantitative lower bounds for trace reconstruction
A uniform decoder achieves quasipolynomial sample and running-time bounds for known fixed rational retention probabilities.
Uniform quasipolynomial-time trace reconstruction
When the deletion probability is at most $n^{-\varepsilon}$ for fixed $\varepsilon>0$, both bounds become polynomial in the input and parameter encoding.
A latest-anchor induction with spectrally compact masks for worst-case trace reconstruction
Gives a deterministic polynomial-time $(1+2/e+\varepsilon)$-approximation for finite rational metric $k$-median with specified candidate facilities, for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$.
Single-exponential recovery
Assuming $P\ne NP$, the optimal infimum approximation factor is $1+2/e$.
Approximation threshold
Proves exponential lower bounds both for complementing two-way nondeterministic finite automata
Nondeterministic complementation lower bound
and for simulating one-way nondeterministic automata by two-way deterministic ones.
Two-way deterministic state lower bound
The latter resolves the Sakoda--Sipser state-succinctness conjecture over growing finite alphabets
Gives a deterministic length-$n$ discrete Fourier transform algorithm using $O(n(\log n)^{1-\delta})$ operations for every $n$, with explicit $\delta=10^{-13}$.
Explicit DFT power saving
The model uses exact complex arithmetic, unrestricted coefficients and a supplied root of unity, and counts scalar preparation and logarithmic-word indexing.
Tensor savings and Fourier circuits

Proves unconditional $n^{\Omega(k)}$ deterministic time lower bounds for joint and separate $k$-dimensional Weisfeiler--Leman equivalence, for sufficiently large fixed $k$ in the specified sequential adjacency-matrix models.
Unconditional time lower bounds
With dimension as input, joint equivalence is EXPTIME-complete even on subcubic graphs
Variable-dimension equivalence
deciding whether refinement identifies a graph is also EXPTIME-complete
Graph-identification complexity
Every regular language over a finite alphabet has a generalized regular expression with at most three nested Kleene stars, allowing union, concatenation and complement over the same alphabet.
Star height at most three
This establishes an absolute bound independent of automaton size, resolving the uniform-boundedness version of the generalized star-height problem.
Gives a uniform randomized classical algorithm for worst-case Subset Sum in ordinary $O(2^{0.49n})$ word-RAM time on polynomial-bit inputs, where $n$ counts the integers.
Subset Sum in Time $O(2^{0.49n})$
The time bound holds on every execution and success probability is at least $2/3$ on every input.
A Low-Space Algorithm for Worst-Case Subset Sum
a one-pass learner with $Ad^2$ persistent bits needs $\Omega_A(d\log(1/\epsilon))$ noiseless Gaussian samples to recover a unit vector to angular error $0<\epsilon\le1/10$ with probability $2/3$
Memory and precision
Computation and randomized updates are unrestricted, but output uses only the terminal state, stopping index and fresh randomness.
Localization costs

Resolves the uniform boundedness assertion in Hilbert's sixteenth problem: the number of isolated periodic orbits of a real planar polynomial vector field is bounded by a finite constant depending only on its degree.
Uniform limit-cycle bounds
For classical quintic Li\'enard systems, the exact maximum is two limit cycles.
Quintic Liénard limit cycles
Resolves the near-boundary Birkhoff conjecture for smooth strictly convex planar billiards of positive curvature.
Billiard rigidity
A continuous physical collar of smooth closed convex caustics also suffices.
Analytic caustic collars
Proves the permanence conjecture for every finite weakly reversible mass-action system with fixed positive rate constants.
Uniform Permanence in Weakly Reversible Mass-Action Systems
Every positive stoichiometric compatibility class, even an unbounded one, has a common compact convex forward-invariant absorbing set.
Boundedness and persistence of weakly reversible mass-action systems
Proves that the billiard flow in every nondegenerate Euclidean triangle with at least one angle irrational relative to $\pi$ is weakly mixing for normalized area times uniform direction.
Weak mixing of triangular billiards with an irrational angle
This strengthens ergodicity on the entire irrational-angle class, with no genericity or Diophantine restrictions.
Ergodicity of triangular billiards with an irrational angle
Proves almost-everywhere convergence of consecutive multiple ergodic averages of every finite length for invertible mixing probability-preserving transformations.
Pointwise Multiple Ergodic Averages for Mixing Transformations
For each fixed tuple of bounded functions, the limit is the product of their integrals, along all positive averaging lengths.
Pointwise convergence of fourfold ergodic averages for mixing transformations

Disproves Hadwiger's conjecture even for fractional coloring: arbitrarily large finite simple graphs with independence number at most two satisfy $\chi_f(G)>h(G)$, where $h(G)$ is the largest clique-minor order.
Hadwiger counterexample
Also disproves the fractional Colin de Verdi\`ere chromatic bound $\chi_f(G)\le\mu(G)+1$.
Colin de Verdière counterexample
In the positive direction, every finite nonempty graph satisfies $\chi_{\mathrm{list}}(G)\le C h(G)$ for a universal constant $C$.
Linear list-coloring bound

Disproves Ryser's covering conjecture by constructing intersecting $(q+1)$-partite, $(q+1)$-uniform hypergraphs with covering number $q+1$, rather than the predicted bound $q$, for every sufficiently large prime $q$.
Balanced prime-order counterexamples
A separate construction over extension fields also disproves Gy\'arf\'as's monochromatic tree-cover conjecture.
Original counterexample
Resolves the Harary--Hill conjecture and Tur\'an's brickyard problem in the Zarankiewicz formulation, determining the crossing numbers of every complete and complete bipartite graph.
Complete graphs
The result proves the optimality of the classical drawings among all plane drawings with continuous edge arcs.
Complete bipartite graphs

Proves the weak pinned Erd\H{o}s distance conjecture: for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, all but $o(n)$ points of any $n$-point planar set determine at least $n^{1-\varepsilon}$ distinct nonzero distances.
Weak pinned planar distances
A complementary theorem bounds the number of unit-distance pairs by $O(n^{4/3-\delta})$ for an absolute $\delta>0$.
Planar unit-distance power saving
For every fixed integer $s\ge5$, proves $r(s,t)=t^{s-1}/(\log t)^{s-2+o(1)}$ as $t\to\infty$, determining the logarithmic exponent and matching the classical upper bound at that scale.
Fixed off-diagonal Ramsey numbers

Resolves the strong thin-tree conjecture constructively. Every finite loopless $k$-edge-connected multigraph on at least two vertices has a spanning tree containing at most a universal $C/k$ fraction of the edges of every cut.
Strong thin tree conjecture
Such a tree can be found deterministically in polynomial time, even with binary-encoded parallel-edge multiplicities.
Polynomial-time construction
Proves that integral and fractional expectation thresholds differ by at most a universal factor
Expectation-threshold equivalence
resolves Talagrand's discrete-convexity conjecture
Discrete convexity
An application proves the Ascoli--He--Park--Talagrand graph-decomposition conjecture
Graph Decompositions at the Integral Expectation Threshold
proves that a subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ avoiding nonzero values $h(1),h(2),\ldots$ as differences has size $O_h(N^{1-c_k})$, with $c_k>0$ depending only on degree
A power saving for intersective polynomial differences with an exponent depending only on the degree
For prime arguments, a power saving also holds when $h$ has a unit root modulo every modulus, with exponent allowed to depend on $h$.
A Power Saving for Polynomial Differences at Prime Arguments

Proves the Alon--Krivelevich--Sudakov coloring conjecture in correspondence-coloring form: graphs avoiding any fixed subgraph $F$ need $O_F(\Delta/\log\Delta)$ colors when their maximum degree $\Delta$ is sufficiently large.
Correspondence coloring graphs with a forbidden clique

Also proves the Ajtai--Erd\H{o}s--Koml\'os--Szemer\'edi independence conjecture: for fixed $r\ge4$, every $n$-vertex $K_r$-free graph of average degree $d\ge2$ has an independent set of size $\Omega_r(n\log d/d)$.
A logarithmic independence bound for clique-free graphs
Proves the Friedgut--Kalai threshold-width conjectures for graphs and fixed-uniformity hypergraphs.
A Sharp Threshold Bound for Monotone Graph Properties
The hypergraph influence bound also applies to nonmonotone properties.
A uniform influence bound for hypergraph properties
Constructs a finitely presented torsion-free nonsofic group whose group algebra over $\mathbb F_2$ is not directly finite, disproving Kaplansky's conjecture even without torsion.
Torsion-free direct-finiteness counterexample
Companion examples give injective nonsurjective cellular automata on all configurations, refuting Gottschalk's surjunctivity conjecture.
Characteristic two

Another counterexample is an integral group-ring matrix, invertible over the rational group ring, with Fuglede--Kadison determinant strictly between zero and one, disproving the unrestricted Determinant Conjecture.
Determinant
disprove the Auslander--Reiten and Gorenstein-projective conjectures
Auslander–Reiten counterexample
and Tachikawa's second conjecture.
Tachikawa’s second conjecture
Proves the Eisenbud--Green--Harris and lex-plus-powers conjectures over every characteristic-zero field.
Artinian lex-plus-powers Betti theorem
Any homogeneous ideal containing a regular sequence, of arbitrary length and degrees at least two, admits a lex-plus-powers ideal with the same Hilbert function and no smaller graded Betti numbers.
Commuting division-coefficient forms

Proves Donovan's conjecture: over each fixed algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$, blocks of finite groups with bounded defect-group order have only finitely many Morita-equivalence classes, for every prime $p$.
Donovan over algebraically closed fields
Also proves the integral form over each fixed complete mixed-characteristic discrete valuation ring with algebraically closed residue field.
Integral Donovan over Witt vectors
Proves Saxl's conjecture: the tensor square of every staircase representation contains every irreducible complex representation of the corresponding symmetric group.
Universal tensor squares
More generally, every $S_n$ with $n\notin\{2,4,9\}$ has an irreducible representation whose tensor square contains all irreducibles.
Cyclic polytabloid proof
Some finite lattices are not congruence lattices of any finite algebra, answering the finite lattice representation problem negatively.
Negative solution
Moreover, no algorithm decides whether a finite lattice has such a representation, or whether it is a full subgroup interval of a finite group.
Characterization and undecidability
Proves the $\ell^1$-Bass conjecture for every discrete group: Hattori--Stallings traces of idempotent matrices over $\ell^1(G)$ are supported on finitely many finite-order conjugacy classes.
The $\ell^1$-Bass Conjecture for Discrete Groups
The algebraic companion proves the integral Bass trace conjecture and Kaplansky's idempotent conjecture for torsion-free groups over every commutative unital characteristic-zero domain.
The Bass trace conjecture and the characteristic-zero Kaplansky idempotent conjecture
Disproves unrestricted integral Gersten injectivity in degrees $3$ and $5$.
Degree-three Gersten counterexample
Two explicit two-dimensional ramified regular local rings of mixed characteristic $(0,5)$ have nonzero integral $K$-theory classes that vanish over their fraction fields.
Integral Gersten counterexample

Proves the sixth case of Foulkes’ conjecture: $\operatorname{Sym}^6(\operatorname{Sym}^bV)$ embeds equivariantly in $\operatorname{Sym}^b(\operatorname{Sym}^6V)$ for every $b\ge6$ and finite-dimensional complex $V$.
Sixth symmetric power

More generally, the canonical multiplication map $\operatorname{Sym}^b(\operatorname{Sym}^aV)\to\operatorname{Sym}^a(\operatorname{Sym}^bV)$ is surjective for $a\ge2$ and $b\ge a(a-1)$, giving dimension-independent quadratic stabilization.
Quadratic stabilization
Critical Fortuin--Kasteleyn planar maps converge to Liouville quantum gravity spheres for $0<q\le4$
Critical sphere at $q=4$
and to the Brownian continuum random tree for $q>4$, establishing the surface-to-tree geometric transition.
Brownian CRT limits for $q>4$
For FK--Ising and spanning-tree-weighted maps, stationary random walks converge to Liouville Brownian motion on the limiting sphere.
Random Walks on Critical FK--Ising Maps and Liouville Brownian Motion
The FK--Ising spectral result also gives convergence of eigenvalues and heat traces, using the stated Brownian/LQG inputs.
Spectral convergence for critical FK--Ising planar maps
Proves that planar first-passage percolation has no doubly infinite geodesic for iid nonnegative nonatomic edge weights when the minimum of four weights has finite second moment.
No bigeodesics
For exponential weights, the limit shape is strictly convex with $C^1$ boundary. Differentiability also holds for every Gamma law with positive shape and rate.
Strict convexity and differentiability

Resolves the Benjamini--Schramm criticality conjecture for bond percolation on every infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive graph with $p_c<1$: at the critical probability, there is almost surely no infinite cluster.
Quasi-transitive graphs at criticality
The family also establishes this conclusion for both nearest-neighbor bond and site percolation on $\mathbb Z^3$.
Cubic-lattice bond and site percolation
Constructs the canonical continuum limit of the two-dimensional nearest-neighbor $O(3)$ model: a non-Gaussian local relativistic theory with a unique vacuum and a positive mass gap.
O(3) massive continuum limit
For the square-lattice $O(4)$ model, determines the exact leading asymptotic of the full transfer gap, $m_{\mathrm{lat}}(\beta)\sim32e^{\pi/4-1/2}\sqrt\beta\,e^{-\pi\beta}$.
Exact mass asymptotics for the two-dimensional $O(4)$ lattice model
The family also proves exponential spin-correlation decay for two-dimensional nearest-neighbor $O(n)$ models with $n\ge3$ at every positive temperature.
O(n) exponential decay
proves critical axis correlations $C_{\beta_c}(r)\sim Ar^{-1/4}(\log r)^{1/8}$
The critical logarithmic correction for the planar XY model
the Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless essential singularity $\sqrt{\beta_c-\beta}\log\xi(\beta)\to B$, with $A,B>0$ after the free-box thermodynamic limit
Essential Singularity of the Correlation Length in the Planar XY Model
discrete Gaussian heights converge to Gaussian fields throughout the rough phase, including its threshold, along geometric torus sizes
Height and spin-field universality
Critical center-magnetization and spin-field conclusions retain their stated height, renormalization, and field-input assumptions.
Critical Center Magnetization in the Planar XY Model
For every fixed inverse temperature $\beta>1$, determines the fluctuation scale and limiting law of the zero-field Gaussian Sherrington--Kirkpatrick log partition function.
Fluctuation scale
Exact centering and standardization give full-sequence convergence to a uniquely characterized nondegenerate law.
Free-energy limiting law
Weak finite-range square-symmetric even multispin perturbations of the square-lattice Ising model preserve critical bulk spin and energy limits
Bulk correlation universality
weak square-symmetric contour interactions also yield chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_3$ interface limits
$\mathrm{SLE}_3$ universality
With sufficiently weak iid bond disorder of any fixed bounded nondegenerate mean-zero law, critical spin interfaces converge to the same law in probability over environments.
Quenched $\mathrm{SLE}_3$ limits for general weak random-bond Ising models
For every fixed degree $d\ge3$, the bulk adjacency-eigenvalue point process of a uniform simple random $d$-regular graph converges to the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble law, including for cubic graphs.
GOE bulk universality for fixed-degree random regular graphs
The same fixed-energy universality persists under sufficiently weak fixed iid uniform diagonal disorder, throughout compact bands strictly inside the clean spectral edges.
Fixed-energy universality for weak Anderson disorder on random regular graphs
On $\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge3$, directional escape has probability zero or one for iid strictly elliptic nearest-neighbor environments
Strict-ellipticity zero–one law
for stationary ergodic finite-range-dependent environments under uniform ellipticity
A directional zero--one law for finite-range-dependent random environments

In iid uniformly elliptic environments with $d\ge2$, almost-sure directional transience implies a deterministic limiting velocity with positive projection in that direction, resolving the ballisticity conjecture.
Directional transience implies ballisticity
Determines finite-temperature variational free energies for Gaussian Ising perceptrons with bounded Borel log-potentials
Ising perceptron free energy
Gaussian spherical perceptrons with bounded continuous potentials, at every positive pattern density
Spherical perceptron free energy
A spherical extension treats bi-orthogonally invariant disorder with compact limiting singular-value distributions and no outliers.
Bi-orthogonally invariant disorder
At margin $-1$, the quadratic-penalty spherical model has a sharp feasibility threshold and limiting gap and force laws
Negative spherical perceptron jamming
Proves chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa$ limits for critical square-lattice random-cluster interfaces for $0<q\le4$, with $\kappa=4\pi/\arccos(-\sqrt q/2)$
Conformal Limits of Critical Square-Lattice Random-Cluster Interfaces
bounded Jordan domains are allowed for $q\ge1$
FK interfaces and nested loops ($1\le q<4$)
smooth Jordan domains for $q<1$
Self-dual interfaces ($q<1$)
Proves Cardy's formula for annealed critical Poisson--Voronoi crossing probabilities in every bounded Jordan quadrilateral.
Cardy’s formula for critical Poisson–Voronoi percolation
This establishes quenched near-critical universality for crossing thresholds.
From critical crossings to quenched near-critical universality in Voronoi percolation
With each model normalized by its own expected unit-square pivotal count
A Pivotal Amplitude for Voronoi Percolation from Cardy's Formula
For zero-field Gaussian SK heat-bath dynamics with rate-one updates per spin, proves worst-start cutoff on the $\log n$ scale for fixed $0\le\beta<1$
High-temperature cutoff
mixing time $n^{2/3+o(1)}$ at $\beta=1$
Critical mixing
and stretched-exponential mixing from a Gibbs-sampled fixed starting configuration for $\beta>1$, in probability over disorder.
Typical-start stretched-exponential barriers
At criticality, rescaled stationary and quench autocorrelation processes have universal random limits for Gaussian and Rademacher disorder; the quench limit relaxes to the stationary limit.
Universality of critical quench autocorrelations in the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model

Constructs stable distance-dependent pair interactions for three-dimensional classical particles with a first-order phase transition: the canonical free energy has a derivative jump at one inverse temperature throughout an open density interval.
Temperature singularity
One potential has a divergent repulsive core; another is bounded and continuous with an integrable power-law tail, realizing the type of transition sought in Simon's continuum problem.
Algebraic-decay phase transition
Proves the exact reconstruction threshold $d\lambda^2>1$, with nonreconstruction at equality, for three-state symmetric and four-state ferromagnetic broadcasting on regular trees
The Reconstruction Threshold for the Ferromagnetic Four-State Potts Model
The three-state theorem allows both signs of $\lambda$ and gives the exact weak-recovery threshold for the symmetric three-community stochastic block model.
The exact reconstruction threshold for the three-state symmetric channel
Resolves Schramm’s Hausdorff-measure question for chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa$, $0<\kappa<8$.
Exact Hausdorff gauge

The explicit gauge $r^d(\log\log(1/r))^{(2-d)/2}$, $d=1+\kappa/8$, gives almost surely positive finite measure to every trace segment $\gamma([s,t])$ with $0<s<t<\infty$, and finite expected measure to the trace in every bounded disk.
Explicit exact Hausdorff gauge
Proves Gaussian free field limits on bounded smooth simply connected domains for triangular-lattice height models
Weighted integer heights
and zero-boundary integer Lipschitz heights weighted by fixed $x\in[1/\sqrt2,1]$
Integer heights with two-arc boundary

Uniform real Lipschitz heights also converge to a Gaussian field; at a tuned opposite-boundary amplitude, their interface converges to chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_4$, establishing Schramm’s real-field/interface predictions.
Uniform real Lipschitz surfaces
For random $k$-SAT with independent uniformly signed proper clauses sampled with replacement, proves finite positive limiting thresholds
Fixed-clause-size limiting threshold
and hitting-time variance $\Theta_k(n)$ for every fixed $k\ge3$
Random k-SAT hitting-time variance
and computability of the 3-SAT threshold.
Computing the random 3-SAT threshold
Proves the diameter form of Nienhuis's predicted three-quarter exponent: a uniformly chosen $n$-step self-avoiding walk on the honeycomb lattice has diameter $n^{3/4+o(1)}$.
Its local mass and covering numbers have exponent $4/3$.
Mass and covering exponents for fixed-length walks
These estimates hold at every sufficiently large fixed length, simultaneously across scales, with arbitrarily high polynomial probability.
Proves that the Thorp shuffle randomizes $N=2^d$ labeled cards in $\Theta(\log N)$ physical shuffles, settling its optimal mixing order for power-of-two deck sizes.
Optimal-order mixing of the Thorp shuffle
Convergence is in total variation from the worst initial ordering and concerns the entire permutation, not just individual card positions.
Determines the sharp exponential singularity rate of symmetric random sign matrices with independent entries on and above the diagonal.
The sharp exponential rate of singularity for symmetric Bernoulli matrices
for fixed bias $p\in(0,1)\setminus\{1/2\}$, the rate is $(p^2+(1-p)^2+o(1))^n$.
The sharp singularity rate for biased symmetric sign matrices
In the biased case, agreeing rows attain this rate.
Proves Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture in ZFC
Eventual categoricity
Under the continuum hypothesis, a proposed specific Hanf threshold need not suffice.
CH threshold obstruction

Confirms the Blass--Gurevich--Shelah noncapture conjecture: consistency of a linear system over $\mathbb F_3$ defines a polynomial-time query on unordered finite structures that choiceless polynomial time with counting cannot express.
Failure to capture polynomial time
A separate result shows that adding witnessed symmetric choice strictly increases expressive power.
Witnessed symmetric choice
Constructs an infinite finitely presented residually finite group whose elements all have finite $2$-power order
An infinite finitely presented periodic group
answering the finitely presented Burnside problem negatively even in this class.
An infinite finitely presented residually finite 2-group
A finitely generated group has decidable word problem exactly when it embeds in a finitely presented simple group, proving the Boone--Higman conjecture.
Simple $F_\infty$ overgroups
A single group of type $F_\infty$ can also contain every finitely presented group.
Universal $F_\infty$ group
Resolves Dixmier's problem for all discrete groups: amenability is equivalent to every uniformly bounded Hilbert-space representation being similar to a unitary representation.
Unitarizability implies amenability for discrete groups

For countable discrete groups, amenability is also equivalent to strong Ulam stability: sufficiently accurate unitary approximate representations are uniformly close in operator norm to genuine representations on the same, possibly infinite-dimensional, Hilbert space.
Strong Ulam Stability Characterizes Amenability
The Salvetti complex of every finite-rank Artin group is aspherical, proving the Artin $K(\pi,1)$ conjecture.
Artin $K(\pi,1)$
Arbitrary intersections of its parabolic subgroups are parabolic, proving the Parabolic Intersection Conjecture.
Parabolic intersections
An explicit Artin group admits no proper cocompact isometric action on any nonempty proper CAT$(0)$ space.
No geometric CAT(0) action

Proves that every finite system of equations over an arbitrary group whose exponent-sum matrix has full row rank over $\mathbb Q$ has a simultaneous solution in an overgroup, resolving Howie's conjecture.
Nonsingular systems of equations over arbitrary groups
A companion proves Kervaire's conjecture: adjoining one generator and one relation cannot trivialize a nontrivial group.
The Kervaire theorem for groups
Proves Gersten's conjecture: every finitely generated one-relator group containing no Baumslag--Solitar subgroup $\mathrm{BS}(m,n)$, with $m,n\ne0$, is word-hyperbolic.
Baumslag–Solitar-free one-relator groups
It also proves that every word-hyperbolic one-relator group is virtually compact special.
Virtual compact specialness

Proves the sharp enclosing-area spacetime Penrose inequality for smooth one-ended asymptotically flat initial data in every spatial dimension $n\ge3$, under dominant energy, weak future trapping, positive enclosing area, and the stated decay assumptions.
Numerical spacetime
It bounds invariant ADM mass below using minimum enclosing area, with equality rigidity under additional horizon hypotheses.
Equality and rigidity
Charged upper-area bounds treat dyonic three-dimensional data;
Three-dimensional charged inequality
the higher-dimensional purely electric extension uses the matched neutral theorem.
Higher-dimensional charged reduction
In dimension two, every positive disorder strength gives almost surely pure-point spectrum.
Pure-point spectrum
In every fixed dimension $d\ge3$, sufficiently weak positive disorder gives purely absolutely continuous spectrum on a fixed open interval with nonzero spectral weight.
Absolutely continuous spectrum
Resolves the predicted spectral contrast for the lattice Anderson model with independent uniform site potentials.
Proves the sharp one-dimensional Lieb--Thirring inequality for $1/2<\gamma<3/2$ and arbitrary finite-matrix potentials $W\ge0$ with $\int\operatorname{tr}(W^{\gamma+1/2})<\infty$
Sharp one-dimensional Lieb--Thirring inequalities for matrix potentials
the optimal constant is the scalar one-bound-state value, independent of matrix size.
Sharp one-dimensional Lieb–Thirring constants
All equality cases are direct sums, in one constant unitary basis, of scalar $\operatorname{sech}^2$ solitons with independent scales and centers, and zero channels.
Equality cases in the sharp one-dimensional matrix Lieb--Thirring inequality
proves that a molecule with $M$ fixed nuclei of charges at least one and total charge $Z$ strictly binds at most $Z+CM$ electrons.
Uniform excess charge and outer radius
Neutral-atom first ionization energies and radii containing all but an expected half-electron have universal positive upper and lower bounds.
Generalized ionization energies
neutral-atom outer radii have the corresponding iterated-limit asymptotics, taking $Z\to\infty$ first.
Generalized outer-electron radii

A dense $G_\delta$ subset of a weighted smooth neighborhood of smooth complete two-ended asymptotically flat vacuum data has full maximal globally hyperbolic developments with no future continuous nondegenerate extension whose weak connection is locally square-integrable.
Future inextendibility, $L^2$ connection

Proves an entropy area law for unique ground states of finite-range Hamiltonians on arbitrary finite induced square-lattice domains, using only a uniform full-system spectral gap and bounds on the local interactions.
Two-dimensional area law

On open $L\times L$ squares, uniformly gapped nearest-neighbor ground states also admit projected entangled-pair state approximations with polynomial bond dimension and global vector error at most $L^{-1}$.
Polynomial PEPS approximation
Proves $N(6)=3$, resolving Zauner\textquotesingle s dimension-six mutually unbiased bases conjecture: three such bases exist in $\mathbb C^6$, but four cannot.
Maximum number of bases
An independent companion proves the Matolcsi--Ruzsa--Weiner Fourier-vanishing conjecture for order-six complex Hadamard matrices outside Tao\textquotesingle s cubic equivalence class.
Exact Fourier certificates

Proves Bose--Einstein condensation for the exact canonical Gibbs state of the three-dimensional hard-sphere gas: each fixed exclusion distance and sufficiently small fixed density admit a strictly positive temperature, independent of volume, with positive condensate fraction in the thermodynamic limit.
Bose--Einstein condensation at positive temperature in the dilute hard-sphere gas

At zero temperature, proves the Bogoliubov leading quantum-depletion law for hard spheres and fixed bounded nonnegative radial finite-range potentials of positive scattering length, taking the thermodynamic limit before the dilute limit.
Quantum Depletion and Momentum Distribution in the Dilute Hard-Sphere Bose Gas

At zero temperature, proves the Bogoliubov leading quantum-depletion law for hard spheres and fixed bounded nonnegative radial finite-range potentials of positive scattering length, taking the thermodynamic limit before the dilute limit.
Quantum Depletion for Fixed Bounded Repulsive Potentials
Proves the spin-one Haldane gap conjecture for the pure antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chain on even periodic rings: the spectral gap stays uniformly positive as the chain grows.
Periodic Haldane gap
A companion establishes a gap for odd open chains with endpoint field $h=3/5$ and gives boundary-selected infinite-volume states with topological index $-1$.
Boundary-field gap
Proves the fermionic Laughlin spectral-gap conjecture for the full $V_1$ interaction at filling $1/3$ on the round sphere.
A Fock-space inequality and the Laughlin spectral gap

The unique ground state remains uniformly gapped under sufficiently weak bounded real scalar one-body potentials projected to the lowest Landau level. Both the gap and disorder threshold are uniform over all sufficiently large particle numbers and all normalized potential profiles.
Uniform Stability of the Spherical Laughlin Gap
Proves that the undeformed relative $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ BFSS model has exactly one normalizable zero-energy state for every finite $N\ge2$, resolving the threshold-bound-state conjecture.
The unique threshold bound state of the SU(N) BFSS model

For $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, a companion proves infinitely many normalizable positive-energy eigenstates with unbounded energies, contradicting the original BFSS paper\textquotesingle s exclusion of additional bound states at $N=2$.
Positive eigenvalues of the relative SU(2) BFSS Hamiltonian

Proves Bloch's $T^{3/2}$ law with its exact coefficient for three-dimensional quantum Heisenberg ferromagnets at every positive quantum spin, allowing nonnegative symmetric finite-range couplings whose support generates $\mathbb Z^3$.
Bloch's Law for Finite-Range Heisenberg Ferromagnets in Three Dimensions
The family also proves spontaneous magnetization for nearest-neighbor models in every dimension $d\ge3$
Spontaneous magnetization in the quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet
and determines the first lattice correction for three-dimensional nearest-neighbor couplings.
The first lattice correction to Bloch's law

Resolves Moore's parity conjecture in the measured-output model: constant-depth quantum circuits with arbitrary one-qubit gates, unbounded-arity Toffoli gates and polynomially many total qubits cannot compute parity with any fixed positive worst-case advantage.
Product-projection localization
Xu--Li's reductions give the same bounded-error obstruction for strict majority.
Regular trajectories and pruning
Proves QMA-hardness of approximating the electronic Coulomb energy infimum in three dimensions, minimizing over the full spinful fermionic continuum space.
Binary nuclear charges
Deterministic polynomial-time reductions work even with only unit-charge nuclei at distinct rational positions, polynomially many electrons and an energy-threshold separation of at least one.
Unit nuclear charges
Proves that QAOA approaches the ground-state energy of the Gaussian zero-field Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model when system size tends to infinity before circuit depth.
QAOA attains the SK ground-state energy in the thermodynamic-first limit
This also yields leading-order optimal expected MaxCut values on large-degree random regular graphs, with size tending to infinity before degree.
Disproves the coefficient-free reduced Baum--Connes conjecture through a failure of rational injectivity and a separate failure of surjectivity of assembly.
Baum–Connes injectivity
Separately, a torsion-free group has a nontrivial projection in its reduced group $C^*$-algebra, disproving the Kadison--Kaplansky conjecture.
Kadison–Kaplansky counterexample
A finitely generated torsion-free example witnesses the injectivity failure.
Irrational-trace Baum–Connes counterexample
Classifies finite-index bimodules between scalar-twisted group factors of ICC groups commensurable with property-$(T)$ lattices over characteristic-zero local fields and arbitrary ICC group factors.
Twisted finite correspondences
The classification also recovers the group, scalar cocycle and amplification scale up to the stated stable equivalence.
Arithmetic category and stable recovery

Proves that sufficiently close unital von Neumann algebras on the same Hilbert space are conjugate by a unitary arbitrarily close to the identity, with a universal tolerance in the operator-norm distance between unit balls.
Universal strong Kadison–Kastler stability
Counterexamples show that near-identity conjugacy fails for one-sided near inclusions
Near Inclusions of von Neumann Algebras Without Small Spatial Embeddings
arbitrarily close norm-separable $C^*$-algebras need not be ambiently unitarily conjugate
Close Separable $C^*$-Algebras Without Spatial Conjugacy
Proves Connes' bicentralizer conjecture for every type $\mathrm{III}_1$ factor with separable predual and every faithful normal state.
Modular spectral averages

More generally, for every inclusion $N\subset M$ of von Neumann algebras with separable preduals admitting a faithful normal conditional expectation, constructs an amenable expected subalgebra $P\subset N$ with $P'\cap c(M)=N'\cap c(M)$, resolving the relative bicentralizer conjecture.
Core-commutant preservation

Proves equivariant Jiang--Su stability for every countable discrete amenable group action on a simple separable unital infinite-dimensional nuclear stably finite Jiang--Su-stable $C^*$-algebra, resolving this case of Szab\'o's conjecture without restrictions on trace dynamics.
Equivariant Jiang--Su Stability for Amenable Actions in the Unital Stably Finite Case

The family also proves the unital Toms--Winter conjecture, equating strict comparison, finite nuclear dimension and Jiang--Su stability in the simple separable unital infinite-dimensional nuclear setting.
Nuclear dimension and Jiang–Su stability
Constructs a nonzero norm-quasinilpotent operator on every infinite-dimensional separable complex Hilbert space with no nonzero proper closed subspace invariant under every commuting operator.
Backward intertwiners and a transitive commutant
The construction also gives operators with no nontrivial invariant projection in the hyperfinite type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor.
Invariant-projection counterexamples for every irrational rotation
Proves that every self-adjoint element of a complex von Neumann algebra admits strong-operator paving relative to any maximal abelian subalgebra with $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ blocks.
Approximation paving
The norm bound holds after compression by a projection arbitrarily close to the identity in the strong topology, resolving the Popa--Vaes quadratic paving conjecture.
Quadratic strong-operator paving
For every minimal homeomorphism $h$ of an infinite compact metrizable space $X$, the radius of comparison of $C(X)\rtimes_h\mathbb Z$ equals $\tfrac12\mathrm{mdim}(X,h)$, including infinite values.
Radius $=\frac12$ mean dimension
Zero mean dimension is equivalent to the small boundary property, Jiang--Su stability and finite nuclear dimension; in this case nuclear dimension is at most one.
Boundary-preserving cobordism compression
The unrestricted four-dimensional disk-embedding conjecture fails: framed algebraic dual spheres do not suffice to obtain disjoint locally flat spanning disks.
Marked tensor obstruction
In particular, the free group $F_2$ is not good in the sense of Freedman--Quinn.
Boundary-only obstruction

Also constructs a finitely presented integral Poincaré duality group of dimension four with a finite classifying space but no realization as the fundamental group of a closed aspherical topological four-manifold, disproving Wall's conjecture.
PD4 group without aspherical manifold model
Constructs a uniformly discrete bounded-geometry space whose maximal coarse assembly map is not rationally injective.
Failure of rational injectivity for maximal coarse assembly
A companion gives the analogous failure for reduced coarse assembly, disproving the rational coarse Novikov conjecture.
A counterexample to the coarse Novikov conjecture
For every $n\ge0$, constructs a finite Smith--Toda spectrum at a prime $p$ depending on $n$, with Brown--Peterson homology $BP_*/(p,v_1,\ldots,v_n)$ and the canonical comodule structure.
Varying primes
Thus Smith--Toda complexes exist at every height when the prime may vary; an explicit example realizes $V(4)$ at $p=1009$.
V(4) at prime 1009
Disproves strong chromatic splitting at height three for primes $p\ge5$, and weak splitting for the derived $p$-completed sphere at heights $p$ ($p\ge5$) and $p+1$ ($p\ge7$).
Weak chromatic splitting counterexamples
for $n\ge1$ and $p>n+1$, the overlap $L_{n-1}L_{K(n)}S_p^\wedge$ admits a $2^n$-stage filtration by the predicted localized-sphere pieces
Filtered splitting at generic primes
At height three and prime three, even finite assembly from such pieces fails in the category of $E(2)$-local modules over the derived completed sphere.
Finite-assembly failure at prime three
Constructs separable real Banach spaces that are globally bi-Lipschitz equivalent but not linearly isomorphic, resolving the separable Lipschitz-isomorphism problem negatively.
Lipschitz equivalence without linear isomorphism
Thus even the complete metric structure up to bi-Lipschitz equivalence does not determine a separable Banach space's linear isomorphism class.
Bi-Lipschitz $c_0$ absorption

Resolves the complete Crouzeix conjecture: for every bounded operator $A$ on a complex Hilbert space and every finite matrix-valued polynomial $P$, one has $\lVert P[A]\rVert\le2\sup_{z\in W(A)}\lVert P(z)\rVert$, where $W(A)$ is the numerical range.
Structural proof
The constant $2$ is sharp, independent of the matrix size, and valid in infinite dimensions.

Constructs a real reflexive Banach space with an asymptotically midpoint uniformly convex norm but no equivalent asymptotically uniformly convex norm, extending Baudier's separation to reflexive spaces.
Reflexive tree-space example

In the same space, depth-$k$ countably branching diamonds require distortion at least $\sqrt{1+k/12}$, so midpoint uniform convexity does not force uniformly bounded diamond distortion even under reflexivity.
Midpoint and tree energies

Proves $\int_M(\mathrm{Scal}_g^-)^{n/2}\,dV_g\ge a_n\lVert M\rVert$ for every closed connected oriented smooth $n$-manifold, $n\ge3$, and every smooth metric, with $a_n>0$ depending only on dimension.
An integral scalar curvature bound for real simplicial volume
Also proves rational inessentiality under positive scalar curvature, resolving the Gromov--Lawson conjecture; every nonnegative-scalar-curvature metric on a closed aspherical manifold is flat.
Positive scalar curvature forces rational inessentiality

Every complete connected smooth boundaryless $n$-manifold, $n\ge3$, satisfying $-4\Delta+\mathrm{Scal}\ge1$ as a quadratic-form inequality admits a continuous map to a simplicial complex of dimension at most $n-2$
Spectral scalar curvature and uniform Urysohn width
Universal covers of closed positive-scalar-curvature manifolds also have continuous macroscopic dimension at most $n-2$ for every $n\ge2$.
Positive scalar curvature and uniform codimension-two width

Proves generalized Cartan--Hadamard isoperimetry in every dimension: in a complete simply connected manifold with sectional curvature at most $\kappa\le0$, every finite-volume finite-perimeter set satisfies the sharp comparison with the equal-volume model ball.
Cartan–Hadamard isoperimetry and rigidity
Bounded positive-volume equality regions for $\kappa=0$ are Euclidean balls.
Also proves sharp Euclidean filling bounds for compactly supported integral $n$-cycles, $n\ge2$, in arbitrary proper CAT$(0)$ spaces.
Sharp integral fillings in CAT(0) spaces
Proves that every stationary integral $m$-varifold in a Euclidean open set has singular set of Hausdorff dimension at most $m-1$, a sharp bound in every positive dimension and codimension.
A Codimension-One Bound for the Singular Set of a Stationary Integral Varifold
On round spheres, the family also proves almost-everywhere regularity: the singular set has zero $m$-dimensional Hausdorff measure.
Almost-everywhere regularity of stationary integral varifolds

Disproves stable-Morse lower bounds for nondegenerate Hamiltonian fixed points: on simply connected closed K\"ahler manifolds of real dimension $22$, the deficit below the stable Morse number is unbounded.
Hamiltonian Fixed Points Below the Stable Morse Number in Dimension Twenty-Two
A separate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of the complex quadric threefold has exactly three fixed points, fewer than the four critical points required of every smooth function.
Three fixed points on the symplectic quadric threefold
Classifies closed connected Einstein four-manifolds with positive Einstein constant and nonnegative sectional curvature
Zero-Plane Rigidity for Einstein Four-Manifolds
up to scaling, their universal Riemannian covers are the round $S^4$, Fubini--Study $\mathbb{CP}^2$, or a product of equal round two-spheres.
Positively curved Einstein four-manifolds

A closed simply connected nonnegatively curved four-manifold is diffeomorphic to one of these whenever the scale-invariant $L^2$ norm of its trace-free Ricci curvature lies below a universal positive constant.
An $L^2$ Einstein Gap for Nonnegatively Curved Four-Manifolds
Proves the sharp $C\sqrt\lambda$ upper bound for nodal length on every fixed smooth closed surface, completing Yau's conjecture there.
Sharp surface nodal length
The upper bound fails for fixed smooth metrics in dimensions three and four, including metrics on $S^3$ arbitrarily close to round.
Smooth upper-bound counterexamples in dimensions 3–4
In dimension five, nodal measure can grow faster than $\lambda^{1/2+\varepsilon_0}$ for some fixed $\varepsilon_0>0$, ruling out even arbitrarily small power losses.
Power-law violations of Yau’s upper bound
Proves that a smooth Ricci flow on a closed four-manifold extends past any finite time at which scalar curvature remains uniformly bounded.
Four-dimensional smooth extension
A higher-dimensional counterexample has bounded scalar curvature but unbounded full curvature at its finite maximal time, disproving the unrestricted scalar-curvature extension conjecture.
Finite-time curvature blowup
Proves that every smooth locally uniformly convex affine-maximal graph of dimension three through nine, complete for its induced Euclidean metric, is an elliptic paraboloid.
The affine Bernstein theorem in dimensions three through nine
A smooth entire nonquadratic example in dimension ten makes this range sharp.
A Smooth Nonquadratic Entire Affine Maximal Graph in Dimension Ten

Proves Gigli's conjecture: in every integer dimension $n\ge2$, Alexandrov curvature at least $\kappa$ is characterized by the full-support $\operatorname{RCD}((n-1)\kappa,n)$ condition with reference measure $\mathcal H^n$ and distributional sectional curvature at least $\kappa$ in the original global test classes.
Distributional curvature characterization
The RCD condition is unreduced.
Weak Hessian bounds
